# Capture, media and transcription integration design

Status: **candidate MVP design, 2026-10-26**. This elaborates the [system architecture](SYSTEM-ARCHITECTURE.md) and [API/state contract](API-STATE-CONTRACT.md). It is a vendor shortlist and an implementation contract, not a vendor purchase, privacy approval, deployed integration or new Lab admission. The first pilot audience is invited mixed software developers. Region, controller, permitted languages, retention, processor terms and budget remain release decisions in [PRIVACY-ACCESS.md](PRIVACY-ACCESS.md).

## Baseline implementation and open source spike

The [open source video review](OPEN-SOURCE-VIDEO-OPTIONS.md) identifies Uppy Webcam/Audio/Dashboard with Uppy Tus and self-hosted tusd/S3 as the first synthetic-media spike for unblurred capture and upload. The [blur design](BLUR-AND-ASSISTANCE-SAFEGUARDS.md) uses a processed stream that must appear in the participant's live preview and in the saved recording; it tests MediaPipe directly without requiring TensorFlow.js. The table below preserves the app-owned capture/multipart design as a fallback until the spike proves the ten-minute assessment flow, assignment-bound upload authorization and exact recovery behavior. Neither path has been implemented or selected for release.

| Boundary | Candidate choice | Why this fits the pilot | Alternative / switching trigger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Browser recording | Spike Uppy Webcam/Audio; retain native `getUserMedia` + `MediaRecorder` adapter if capture constraints fail | Reuse camera/microphone UI where it satisfies the assessment timer and modes. Capability and MIME still need runtime checks. [Uppy Webcam](https://uppy.io/docs/webcam/), [MDN recorder](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaRecorder) | Thin native capture module if Uppy cannot enforce the exact case/timer flow, especially on mobile. |
| Browser transfer | Spike Uppy Tus + self-hosted tusd/S3; retain app-owned S3 multipart as fallback | Reuses resumable upload protocol and server while the app still owns assignment, verified media receipt and cleanup. Tusd adds an upload service and its resumable URL is a bearer capability. [Uppy Tus](https://uppy.io/docs/tus/), [tusd](https://tus.github.io/tusd/), [tusd hooks](https://tus.github.io/tusd/advanced-topics/hooks/) | App-owned multipart when tusd auth/operations fail the spike; Uppy AwsS3 v6 would require a deliberate custody change because its browser performs completion. |
| Production media store | Private Amazon S3 bucket for first candidate deployment, behind an `ObjectStore` interface | S3 multipart, IAM, lifecycle and checksums cover the needed workflow; it keeps initial batch transcription in one provider. The actual region/account and encryption/key policy require owner approval. [AWS upload integrity](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/checking-object-integrity-upload.html) | Cloudflare R2 if region, operational or measured cost requirements favor it. R2 supports S3 multipart but has API differences, so rerun the conformance suite. [R2 upload](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/objects/upload-objects/), [R2 compatibility](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/s3/api/) |
| Local media store | S3-compatible test service with synthetic clips; no real participant media in developer machines | Exercises the same upload/commit interface without cloud credentials. Select and pin its image/license during B0. | Filesystem fake for unit tests only; it cannot prove browser CORS or multipart behavior. |
| Structured state | PostgreSQL for assignments, consent, upload attempts, media receipts, outbox and lineage | Matches transactional and replay requirements already defined in [DATA-MODEL.md](DATA-MODEL.md). | A managed PostgreSQL host is a deployment choice, not a data-model change. |
| Media validation | Isolated worker using `ffprobe` plus a decoder test and independent digest/size check | The browser's claimed MIME or duration is not authoritative. Probe container, streams and duration after storage commit. [ffprobe](https://ffmpeg.org/ffprobe.html) | Replace the tool if a validated media service offers equivalent evidence and failure codes. |
| First ASR adapter | Amazon Transcribe **batch**, invoked only after verified upload, with output directed to a private controlled bucket | It reads S3 input; WebM and MP4 are among batch inputs, and English and Brazilian Portuguese are supported. Keep exact job/configuration, output and date; record a provider model version only if exposed. [AWS input](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/how-input.html), [languages](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/supported-languages.html) | Evaluate self-hosted `faster-whisper` on an approved research subset if data location, quality or cost warrants it. It needs compute and model operations. [Project](https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper) |
| Scoring model | `ScorerAdapter` behind the existing shadow-mode scoring run; no vendor selected here | This decision depends on the E03/E05 rubric and error studies. Never send raw video by default. | Choose only after versioned evaluation of evidence loss, reliability, latency, cost and processor terms. |

**Vendor posture:** S3 + Transcribe is the proposed coherent first production *candidate*, not an approved deployment. Cloudflare R2 is a storage alternative; Mux direct uploads are a managed video alternative, but its processing and asset model add a recipient and workflow the transcript-led pilot does not yet need. [Mux direct upload docs](https://www.mux.com/docs/guides/upload-files-directly) describe browser and resumable uploads. Do not use a public video hosting URL or an unrestricted media bucket.

### SDK and API shortlist

The browser and API rows below describe the app-owned S3 fallback. The Uppy/Tus spike replaces its browser part transport and signer with Uppy packages and tusd, while retaining the app's session, receipt, verification and deletion contracts. Do not combine both transfer protocols in one production attempt.

| Runtime | SDK/API | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser | Web MediaDevices, MediaRecorder, Web Crypto, IndexedDB and `fetch` | Capture, local recovery aid, digest and direct part transfer. No cloud SDK or long-lived cloud credentials in the browser. |
| TypeScript API/worker | [`@aws-sdk/client-s3`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSJavaScriptSDK/v3/latest/client/s3/), [`@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSJavaScriptSDK/v3/latest/Package/-aws-sdk-s3-request-presigner/) | Create/list/complete/abort multipart uploads and issue narrowly scoped part/read URLs. Keep the S3 commands behind `ObjectStore`. |
| Worker | [`@aws-sdk/client-transcribe`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-javascript/v3/developer-guide/javascript_transcribe_code_examples.html) | Submit and inspect batch jobs through `AsrAdapter`. |
| Worker image | [`ffprobe`](https://ffmpeg.org/ffprobe.html) and a pinned media decoder | Validate the committed object and extract audio when an alternate ASR adapter needs it. |
| API/worker | PostgreSQL driver and migration tool, selected and pinned at B0 | Persist state and transactional outbox. No queue vendor is necessary for the first pilot. |

Dependency versions belong in the future lockfile and release manifest. No package is installed or selected to a version by this design.

## Capture and upload protocol

1. Before `start`, show the approved purpose/notice, request camera and microphone permission in HTTPS, run a non-scored device check, and select a supported MIME with `MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported()`. Do not assume WebM or MP4 works on every target browser. [MDN MIME detection](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaRecorder/isTypeSupported_static)
2. `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/start` fixes the server deadline and reveal schedule. The browser displays it and stops capture at the limit. Record client monotonic timestamps for diagnostics; server events and verified media duration govern acceptance. `MediaRecorder` timeslices are not an accurate clock. [MDN data events](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaRecorder/dataavailable_event)
3. Store ordered recorder blobs under a random local attempt ID while recording. Quota failure or device loss becomes a visible technical failure path. A tab/browser close may end capture; do not promise recovery of an unfinished recording. The audio-only, text and diagram alternatives use the same session/consent state and separate response-mode labels. The [recovery protocol](RECOVERY-PROTOCOL.md) distinguishes interrupted capture from interrupted upload.
4. After stop, form one ordered media `Blob` and calculate its byte size and SHA-256 in the browser. For the first implementation, upload **after** recording, with resumable multipart parts (target 8–16 MiB, tuned by browser tests). Uploading while recording is an experiment if the post-record wait proves too high; it requires proving byte order and container validity on each supported browser. Multipart parts are byte ranges of the **one final media object**, not independently playable clips.
5. The API owns `CreateMultipartUpload`, object key and part-number range. It issues short-lived part URLs for an authorized session and records an `upload_attempt`. The browser sends parts directly, persists successful part receipts locally and asks the API for fresh URLs after expiry. Bucket CORS permits only the pilot origin and required methods/headers. A presigned URL is a bearer capability and stays out of logs and analytics. [AWS presigned URLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/PresignedUrlUploadObject.html)
6. `media-commit` lists parts from storage, checks expected count/order/size, completes multipart server-side once, then probes the stored object. Validate allowed container/codec, decodability, at least one audio stream, bounded video duration, nonempty audio and byte ceiling. Compare the independent stored-object digest with the browser declaration; **do not treat a multipart ETag as a whole-file SHA-256**. S3 supports checksum mechanisms, but the exact SDK algorithm must be pinned and tested for the selected store. [AWS checksum semantics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/checking-object-integrity-upload.html)
7. On valid receipt, transition to `uploaded` and enqueue ASR through the transactional outbox. On invalid/corrupt media, keep the failure and retry lineage, clean up the object under policy, and never assign a zero score. Abort abandoned multipart uploads with API cleanup and a bucket lifecycle rule. [AWS multipart lifecycle](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mpuoverview.html)

The proposed bitrate budget is a **test input**, not a policy: ten minutes at a combined 1–2 Mb/s is roughly 75–150 MB. Run actual browser/device/network measurements before setting `max_bytes`, upload timeouts, resolution and supported-browser policy. The session's ten-minute limit concerns recorded answer duration; upload and transcription may finish later.

## Interface and records to add in B0–B3

| Contract | Minimum fields / actions |
| --- | --- |
| `CaptureAdapter` | `probeDevices`, `selectMime`, `start`, `stop`, `abort`, ordered chunks, client timing/error events; no storage credentials. |
| `ObjectStore` | `createMultipart`, `signPart`, `listParts`, `completeMultipart`, `abortMultipart`, `head`, `readForWorker`, `delete`, `signPurposeBoundRead`. AWS implementation first; same tests for every alternative. |
| `AsrAdapter` | `submit(media_object, language/config version)`, `pollOrReceive`, `fetchResult`, `cancelIfSupported`; outputs time-aligned text, any available confidence/uncertainty metadata and exact submitted configuration. A provider model version is retained only if the provider exposes it. Treat vendor job data and output as separate deletion targets. |
| `upload_attempt` | Assignment, object key, provider/region, upload ID, selected MIME, declared size/hash, part plan and receipts, issued/expiry times, state, error, cleanup deadline, idempotency key. Never persist presigned URLs. |
| `media_object` | Exact upload attempt, storage version/key, verified size/duration/container/codecs, checksum algorithm/value, probe tool version, verification time, retention class and deletion state. Preserve existing [data-model fields](DATA-MODEL.md). |
| `transcription_job` | Media hash, provider/region, job ID, language, submitted configuration and any exposed model version, submitted/completed time, status/error, output object, deletion status. Its result creates a new `transcript_version`; no overwrite on correction or rerun. |

Refine the existing `media-upload` and `media-commit` endpoints with `POST /media-upload/{attempt}/parts:sign`, `GET /media-upload/{attempt}` and `POST /media-upload/{attempt}:abort`; keep one server-owned completion. The exact route shape can change during implementation, but the ownership and idempotency rules cannot. A versioned upload protocol is needed because one presigned single-object PUT cannot provide the chosen multipart resume behavior.

## Research and operational evidence

| Test / measure | Release or research use |
| --- | --- |
| Browser/device matrix: desktop/mobile Chrome, Safari and Firefox; permission denial, codec selection, background/lock, low storage | Decide supported clients and alternate modes. Record `capture_failure` denominator by browser and response mode. |
| Network interruption, URL expiry, reordered/duplicate parts, refresh after stop, slow upload | Prove one committed object and one session receipt; track upload completion, p50/p95 wait and technical-failure rate. |
| Corrupt/oversized/wrong-codec/over-time media; silent audio | Prove server rejection, retry/void path and no ASR/scoring job. |
| Transcript comparison with blind human reference for English/Portuguese and technical terms | E03/E05 measurement: word/content loss, criterion-relevant omissions and subgroup/mode differences; candidate correction remains a separate version. |
| Storage/ASR costs and deletion exercise | Measure object bytes, multipart orphan count, ASR minutes, worker time and complete deletion across raw/derived/vendor output; select region and retention with owners. |

The Lab receives only source-pinned study designs, run/evidence/results and decisions through its existing boundary. An operational `upload_attempt` or vendor job is a product record, not a Lab research result. Link any experiment about capture mode, ASR engine or upload reliability to the protocol version, population, media/ASR configuration and outcome definition before collecting research data.
